messages.subject: Higher-Order CFA
parts:
Hello!

 As I read the examples in the documents, the higher-order CFA is fitted with two orders.  I have a third-order framework to verify.  Could I use {lavaan} to fit such a model?  The data is also nested with group effect.  Is there any small examples to demonstrate how this could be done? 

Thanks,
Xiaomeng

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Higher-Order CFA
parts: I have a third-order framework to verify.  Could I use {lavaan} to fit such a model?
Defining a 3rd-order factor is no different than defining a 2nd-order factor.
The data is also nested with group effect.  Is there any small examples to demonstrate how this could be done?

If there are only a few groups, you can fit a multiple-group model, 

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/groups.html

or a MIMIC model with dummy codes representing all but the reference group.

http://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/cat.html (read about Exogenous Categorical Variables at the top).

If you have several groups, you can account for nesting using the lavaan.survey package

http://daob.nl/wp-content/uploads/2013/03/lavaan-survey.pdf
